title: Smoke in the waiting room
body: Two psychologists invited university students to a laboratory, telling them they would be interviewed. Each student was sent to a waiting room to fill in a questionnaire. Some students sat alone; some sat with two other naive students; and some sat with two people who had secretly been told by the researchers to do nothing. Soon smoke started entering the room through a wall vent, and within four minutes it interfered with vision and breathing. The researchers recorded how often students left the room to report the smoke. About 75 per cent of those waiting alone reported it, groups of three naive students reported it 38 per cent of the time, and only 10 per cent of students sitting with the two instructed people reported it. The speed and amount of smoke and the physical conditions of the rooms were kept the same, and students were assigned to rooms randomly.
